info.title: GrooveSheet Audio Service
info.description:
Audio processing service behind GrooveSheet (https://www.groovesheet.net): stem
separation and transcription to sheet music and MIDI, plus the song library.
Developer docs: https://www.groovesheet.net/developers. MCP server: https://api.groovesheet.net/mcp (signed in) and https://api.groovesheet.net/mcp/public.
SDK and CLI: `npm i @groovesheet/sdk` (`npx @groovesheet/sdk search "easy on me"`), source at https://github.com/groovesheet/groovesheet-sdk.

## Getting started, with no human in the loop

1. **No credential**: the song library (`GET /library/tracks?q=...`, `GET /library/tracks/{id}`,
   `POST /library/tracks/batch`), `/workflows`, `/status` and this document answer without a token.
2. **Sandbox**: `https://api.groovesheet.net/sandbox` is a second server (see `servers`). Every read route works there
   unchanged, and `POST https://api.groovesheet.net/sandbox/workflow/{workflow_name}` runs the whole
   202 -> poll -> download loop with a simulated job that completes in about 15 seconds with the
   real outputs of a fixed demo song. No token, no account, nothing charged, nothing stored
   beyond the job record (24 hours). Build and test against it first.
3. **A free account and a token**: sign up at https://www.groovesheet.net/signup (free; the free tier gives a
   30-second preview of any song and the whole library). A token comes from OAuth 2.1 with
   dynamic client registration at `https://api.groovesheet.net/oauth/register` (open, no approval) or, for
   an agent that cannot open a browser, verified-email registration at `/agent/identity`
   (https://www.groovesheet.net/auth.md). There is no separate API key.
4. **Production**: full songs are paid for in minutes of audio from the account's plan or
   top-up (https://www.groovesheet.net/pricing). `POST /workflow/{workflow_name}` charges before queueing.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. OAuth 2.1 with PKCE (S256):
authorization server metadata at `https://api.groovesheet.net/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`
(issuer `https://api.groovesheet.net`; endpoints `/oauth/register`, `/oauth/authorize`,
`/oauth/token`, `/oauth/userinfo`, `/oauth/jwks`),
protected-resource metadata at `https://api.groovesheet.net/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`. Every `401` carries
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://api.groovesheet.net/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`.
Scopes offered by the authorization server: `openid`, `email`, `profile`,
`offline_access`. Access is per account; tokens carry no finer-grained scopes.

## Long-running work

`POST /workflow/{workflow_name}` and `POST /workflow/{workflow_name}/from-keys`
answer `202 Accepted`: the job is queued, not finished. The body carries the job
id (`workflow_id`) and `status_url`; the `Location` header holds the same URL.
Poll `GET /workflow/status/{workflow_id}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`
(every few seconds is plenty), then fetch outputs from `/workflow/download/...`.

## Retrying safely: Idempotency-Key

Send `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` on `POST /workflow/{workflow_name}`,
`POST /workflow/{workflow_name}/from-keys`, `POST /preview/{workflow_name}`
and `POST /preview/{workflow_name}/from-url`. The same key from the same caller
within 24 hours returns the first response (with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`)
instead of starting, and charging for, the work again. Same key with a different
request: `422`. Same key while the first request still runs: `409` with
`Retry-After`. Failed requests are not remembered, so a retry runs again.

## Batch requests

`POST /library/tracks/batch` with `{"ids": ["<uuid or slug>", ...]}` (up to 50) returns the
same records as `GET /library/tracks/{id}` in one round trip, in the order asked, with `null`
for an id that does not exist or is not visible. `POST /workflow/status/batch` with
`{"workflow_ids": [...]}` (up to 50, signed in) returns the status of each of the caller's jobs,
so a client polling several uploads makes one request per interval instead of one per job.

## Rate limits

Every response carries the IETF `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and
`RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the window resets) headers, and
`RateLimit-Policy` (`<limit>;w=<window seconds>`), for the caller's overall
budget (about 1200 requests per 60 s per client). Some routes
have tighter limits of their own. When a limit is hit the answer is `429` with
`Retry-After` (seconds) and `RateLimit-Remaining: 0`; wait that long and retry.

## Versioning and deprecation

This is version `2` of the API (`info.version`), served at the root with no
version prefix. Every response carries `API-Version: 2`. Clients may send
the optional `API-Version` request header; an unknown version is refused with
`400` and the supported list. Compatible changes (new routes, new optional
fields or parameters) ship without a version change. A breaking change ships as a
new version, announced at least 90 days ahead; until it is withdrawn the old
behaviour keeps working.

Deprecation policy (`x-sunset-policy` in `info`, written out at https://www.groovesheet.net/developers/docs/api#versioning-and-deprecation):

- A route or field that is going away is marked `deprecated: true` in this document on the
  day it is announced, and every response from it carries `Deprecation: @<unix time>`
  (RFC 9745, the announcement date), `Sunset: <HTTP date>` (RFC 8594, the removal date) and
  `Link: <...>; rel="deprecation"` to the policy page plus `rel="successor-version"` to the
  replacement when there is one.
- The sunset date is at least 90 days after the deprecation date. Until then the route
  behaves as before. After it, the route answers `410 Gone` with the successor in the body.
- Changes are listed at https://www.groovesheet.net/changelog and in this document's `x-deprecations`.
- Currently deprecated: `GET /service-status` (use `GET /status`), sunset 6 February 2027.

## Sandbox

`https://api.groovesheet.net/sandbox` (the second entry in `servers`). GET routes are the production ones with the
prefix stripped (the response carries `X-Sandbox: true`). `POST /sandbox/workflow/{workflow_name}`
(multipart `file`, or `/from-keys` with JSON) accepts anything, needs no `Authorization`, and
answers `202` with a `workflow_id` that becomes `completed` after about 15 seconds;
`GET /sandbox/workflow/status/{id}` and `GET /sandbox/workflow/download/{id}/{file_key}`
then serve the demo song's real notation, MIDI and stems under the same `outputs.files` keys the
production workers use. Sandbox job ids start with `SBX` and expire after 24 hours. Nothing in
the sandbox spends minutes or creates an account.

## Errors

Errors are JSON: `{"detail": "..."}` (validation errors: a list under `detail`).
Unknown paths answer `404` with a JSON body pointing here, or Markdown when the
request sends `Accept: text/markdown`.

x-sunset-policy.summary: A route going away is marked deprecated here and answers with Deprecation and Sunset headers for at least 90 days before it stops; then it answers 410 Gone naming the successor.

x-deprecations.note: Replaced by GET /status (public pool status) and GET /status/history.

post.description:
Start a simulated transcription or separation job without a token or minutes.

Same request shape as `POST /workflow/{workflow_name}` (multipart `file`, optional
`metadata` JSON string). The job is not run: it completes on a timer with the demo
song's outputs, so the client can exercise the 202 -> poll -> download loop end to end.

Without query params, returns the legacy {"workflow_ids": [...]} shape.
With ?limit/?offset, returns enriched card items (status, visibility,

post.description:
Start a workflow without uploading a file, for jobs that operate on
R2 objects already present (e.g. `compress_stems` reading existing Demucs
stem WAVs). The first worker reads its inputs from `metadata` instead of
the conventional `input_file`. No audio-duration credit is charged because
no source audio is provided here.

`metadata.input_file` extends this to the transcription workflows: pass an
R2 object key (workers resolve a bare key directly) and a `*_transcribe_*`
chain runs against a stem already in the bucket, no download-and-re-upload
round trip, which is what the library backfill needs. Keep it operator-only:
it reads an arbitrary key in the bucket and bills nothing.

post.description:
The status of several of the caller's jobs in one request.

Body `{"workflow_ids": [...]}` (up to 50). Answer `{"results": [...]}` in the same
order: each entry is what `GET /workflow/status/{workflow_id}` returns, or
`{"workflow_id": ..., "error": {"status": 404 | 403, "detail": ...}}` for a job that
does not exist or belongs to someone else. One poll per interval for a batch of uploads.

get.description: Get workflow status and results. Users can only access their own workflows.

Render the transcription's score to a paginated PDF.

MusicXML is an interchange format, it needs an editor to look at. The PDF
is the copy you can print or put on a stand, so it ships alongside the
MusicXML on every completed transcription.

The transcription's score as a Guitar Pro 5 file.

Drummers, bassists and guitarists read tab in Guitar Pro, Songsterr,
TuxGuitar or MuseScore; .gp5 opens in all of them. Converted from the same
MusicXML the PDF is engraved from, on request (it takes well under a
second, so nothing is cached).
Download a specific output file from a completed workflow.
Download all output files from a completed workflow as a ZIP.

post.description:
Publish (public/unlisted) or unpublish (private) a workflow's library track (§4.2).

Publishing also makes the track usable publicly: sets publish dates + a
stable slug, transcodes WAV stems to streamable formats under the track's
snapshot prefix, and renders a preview image for MIDI tracks. The response
carries `processing: true` while the transcode is in flight.

patch.description: Edit a workflow's display metadata, mirroring to the library track (§4.3).

delete.description:
Delete a workflow and its R2 outputs (§4.4).

Published tracks are a snapshot the public page depends on: unless the
caller passes delete_track=true, a public/unlisted track survives the
workflow deletion (it just loses its workflow link), and any R2 object
still referenced by a kept library asset is preserved. Private tracks are
deleted with the workflow as before.

parameters.name: delete_track

schema.description: For published tracks: true also removes the public track; false/omitted keeps it on Explore (default keeps it).
schema.title: Delete Track

parameters.description: For published tracks: true also removes the public track; false/omitted keeps it on Explore (default keeps it).

Make sure a signed-in user has their account row. Idempotent.

The frontend calls this once per browser session after sign-in. The row
used to appear only on the first account page view, paid run or checkout,
so most people who signed in to browse or download from /explore never got
one (26 rows for 179 Supabase users on 2026-10-21), and credits, email
preference links and anything else keyed on the row missed them.

get.description:
Return all available subscription plans and top-up packs.

Prices are quoted in USD, or in CNY when Cloudflare geolocates the caller
to mainland China. `?currency=` overrides that (used by the currency
toggle) and the chosen currency is echoed in the response so the frontend
can send it back at checkout.

Return the default card on the user's Stripe customer (§3.1).

404 when the user has no Stripe customer or no saved card, the FE hides
the Payment-method section until this returns 200 with data.

post.description: Admin-only: set a plan without payment. Real subscriptions go through Stripe checkout.
Admin-only: grant a top-up without payment. Real top-ups go through Stripe checkout.

Create a Stripe Checkout Session for the signed-in user and return its URL.

Flow:
  1. Resolve the requested plan key to a Stripe price ID + checkout mode.
  2. Look up the user's stored Stripe customer ID, creating one if missing.
  3. Create a Checkout Session with Managed Payments enabled (per the
     blueprint, requires API version 2026-02-25.preview).
  4. Return the session ID + URL. The frontend redirects the browser there.

Chinese traffic (per Cloudflare's CF-IPCountry, so the browser must call
api.groovesheet.net directly, not through Vercel's /api) is checked out
in yuan on a Chinese-language Checkout page, and top-ups also offer Alipay
and WeChat Pay. Both wallets are one-time only, Stripe doesn't support
them in Checkout's subscription mode, so plans stay card-only.

Stripe sends `checkout.session.completed` to /billing/webhook once the
customer pays, that's where we actually credit the account.

Checkout for a visitor who isn't signed in. Stripe collects the email.

The account is found or created for that email once the payment settles
(webhook, or POST /billing/guest-claim from the success page, whichever
comes first). See services/guest_checkout.py for who gets signed in.

The success page of a guest checkout: make sure the minutes are there.

Credits the session if the webhook hasn't yet (both are idempotent, see
fulfil_checkout_session), and returns a one-time sign-in token when the
account was created by this session and never signed into. Otherwise it
names the address, and the buyer signs in as usual.

Create a Stripe Billing Portal session for the signed-in user.

Lets a subscribed user self-manage/cancel their subscription and update
their card on a Stripe-hosted page. Returns the portal URL; the frontend
redirects the browser there.

Requires the user to have a stored Stripe customer ID, i.e. they must
have gone through checkout at least once. Free users who never checked
out get a 409 with a clear message instead of an opaque Stripe error.

NOTE: the Billing Portal must be activated once in the Stripe dashboard
(Settings -> Billing -> Customer portal -> Save) before this works in a
given mode; otherwise Stripe returns an error on the first call.

Cancel the signed-in user's subscription (Airwallex in-app cancel path).

Airwallex has no hosted portal, so this replaces the Stripe Billing Portal's
cancel action. Stripe users still cancel via the portal.

get.description:
What this Checkout Session actually charged, verified against Stripe.

The success page needs the real amount to report a conversion value to
Google Ads. It cannot be trusted to compute one: the price shown depends on
presentment currency and any discount, and a number carried in the redirect
URL is attacker-controlled. So the page asks here and we read it back from
Stripe, refusing sessions that belong to somebody else.

Revenue actually collected, for comparison against ad spend.

Every paid checkout writes `amount_cents`, `currency` and (when the visitor
arrived on an ad) `gclid` onto its credit transaction, so the money can be
totalled here rather than reconstructed from Stripe by hand. `ad_attributed`
counts only payments carrying a Google click id -- the subset whose
acquisition cost is actually known -- which is what makes a
return-on-ad-spend number honest instead of assumed.

post.description:
Payment webhook receiver (Stripe or Airwallex, by provider).

Verifies the signature when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set (production),
and falls back to JSON parsing in dev when it isn't.

Handled events:
    checkout.session.completed       -> credit account, store subscription_id
    customer.subscription.deleted    -> downgrade to free
    invoice.payment_failed           -> log (extend with email/notification later)
The same, for a visitor who isn't signed in: the account follows the payment.
The return page asks: did it go through? Credits it if the webhook hasn't.

A guest's success page after Airwallex: like POST /billing/guest-claim.

Credits the intent if the webhook hasn't, and hands a one-time sign-in
token only to the account this payment created (guest_checkout.may_sign_in).

Open an upload sent in pieces (see services/chunked_uploads.py).

JSON body: ``{"size": <bytes>, "filename": ..., "content_type": ...}``.
Answers ``{"upload_id", "chunk_size", "chunks"}``. Opening one costs no
preview; the preview limit applies when POST /preview/{workflow} starts it.

post.description:
Preview the same song again with another workflow (another instrument).

For "this song has no piano, try drums": the upload is already stored, so
the visitor doesn't send it again. On 2026-10-12 a visitor's re-upload for
exactly this failed three times on their connection and they left.

get.description:
Status + outputs of a preview. Authorized for the originating session
(anonymous cookie) or the owning user (after sign-up + claim).

Paginated PDF of a preview's score, the workflow endpoint's twin.

Previews are the anonymous funnel, so the teaser hands over the same
print-ready file a signed-in transcription does (just of the 10s excerpt).
Stream a single output asset from a completed preview.

post.description:
Transfer an anonymous preview's ownership to the calling user.

Triggered by the frontend right after a successful sign-up. Idempotent:
repeated calls return the same row. Also grants the one-time signup
credit bonus on the first claim per user (independent of preview count).

Body (optional): ``{"offer": "get_free"}`` when the visitor signed up by
tapping the Free plan's "Get Free" after a preview. Then a new account
(under two hours old) that never had one gets the credits to run THIS
preview's whole song (at most 10 minutes), once per user ever, and the
response says so: ``song_credit_granted`` (bool) and ``song_credit_minutes``
(int, minutes of audio, rounded up; 0 when not granted) are always present.
A retried claim of a preview that already got it answers the same again.
A failed grant never fails the claim.

Authorization rules:
  - Caller must be authenticated (Supabase JWT).
  - Either the inbound gs_anon cookie matches preview.anon_session_digest
    (normal path), OR the row is unclaimed and was created within the
    last CLAIM_GRACE_MINUTES (cookie-cleared recovery path).

Run the full (non-preview) workflow against the retained upload.

No re-upload required, we re-use the original file the user dropped
when they generated the preview. Requires the user to own the preview
(post-claim) and to have enough credits for the full song's duration.

One preview buys one full run. A second request for the same preview gets
the run that is already going (or done) instead of a second charge: on
2026-10-17 a buyer's tap and the after-checkout resume landed 2 ms apart
and paid for the song twice.

Public catalog browse + search.

Two pagination modes:
  * default, cursor over published_at desc, for the Explore hub's endless
    "Load More". Browse only: a rank-ordered search can't be resumed from a
    published_at cursor.
  * `page=N`, offset pagination with `total`/`pages`, for the numbered
    results page. Rank order is stable across offsets, so this is the mode
    that may be combined with `q` and any `sort`.

get.description:
Detail view for a public/unlisted track or an owned private track.
Accepts the track UUID or its public slug.

For public and unlisted (link-shared) tracks each asset carries an inline
`stream_url` (presigned R2 GET, 15 min) for streamable formats; lossless
masters (wav/flac) get `stream_url: null` and remain behind the
authenticated download path. Private tracks keep `stream_url: null`
everywhere, owners go through `/library/assets/{id}/url` with auth.

post.description:
Several track details in one request.

The body is `{"ids": [...]}` with up to 50 UUIDs or slugs. The answer is
`{"tracks": [...]}` in the same order, each entry the record
`GET /library/tracks/{track_id}` would return, or `null` for an id that
does not exist or is not visible to the caller. One request instead of
fifty for an agent that has a list of ids from a search.

get.description:
Return a 302 redirect to a presigned R2 URL for the asset.

`format=json` returns `{"url": ...}` instead. The browser ZIP (gs-fe
lib/libraryDownload.ts) needs it: following the 302 from our origin to R2
with an Authorization header failed on every Safari download on
2026-10-13 (Safari either keeps the header, which R2 rejects and refuses
to preflight, or sends `Origin: null`, which R2's CORS rule does not
answer). Fetching the signed URL directly is a plain CORS GET everywhere.

`purpose=stream`, public, returns a short-lived URL (5 min). For public
tracks only streamable formats (mp3/opus/mid/musicxml/json) are allowed;
lossless masters (wav/flac) require the authenticated download path.

`purpose=download`, requires sign-in. Returns a longer-lived URL (1 hour).

Engrave a MusicXML asset to PDF and redirect to it.

/explore has always told visitors the score is "downloadable as PDF and
MusicXML" while only offering the MusicXML, a file most people cannot
open, and cannot put on a music stand. Same visibility rules as streaming
the MusicXML itself, plus sign-in, like every other library download.
`format=json` returns `{"url": ...}`, which the song page needs because a
tab opened with window.open() cannot carry the Authorization header.

Rendering a long score is seconds of CPU, so the result is cached in R2
beside the source and every later request is a redirect like any other
asset. The cache key is derived from the score's own key, so re-running a
transcription (which writes a new key) produces a new PDF rather than
serving a stale one.

Convert a MusicXML asset to Guitar Pro 5 and redirect to it.

Guitar Pro is what drummers, bassists and guitarists open (Guitar Pro,
Songsterr, TuxGuitar and MuseScore all read .gp5); MusicXML means little
to most of them. Same visibility and sign-in rules as the PDF, the same
`format=json` option, and cached in R2 the same way.

post.description:
Record an engagement event (currently only 'play'). Anonymous-capable;
deduped per (track, viewer) per hour so replays don't inflate counters,
and rate-limited per IP so rotating identities can't flood the counters
or mint unbounded Redis keys. Downloads are counted server-side at the
download endpoints instead.

Report a published track (copyright / abuse). Anonymous-capable; one
report per viewer per track. At _REPORT_UNLIST_THRESHOLD distinct
reporters a public track is automatically unlisted pending review, this
is the launch DMCA path until an admin review surface ships.

get.description:
A library file with GrooveSheet's credit and the downloader's ID stamped in.

The token (services/download_marks.make_token) is minted by the download
routes for a signed-in user and expires after an hour, like the R2 URLs it
replaces. No Authorization header: the browser ZIP fetches it with
credentials omitted, as it did R2. Stamping is deterministic, so a resumed
download's `Range` (one range, as lib/libraryDownload.ts sends) lines up.

Download every asset of a track as one ZIP. Sign-in required (parity
with the per-asset download path); visibility-gated like the detail view.

post.description:
Idempotently reserve the Explore record for `spotify_id`.

Repeated calls return the same UUID, the same slug, and the same canonical
URL. Concurrent calls collapse onto one row through the `spotify_id` unique
index. The slug is assigned in the same transaction that creates the row, so
a record is never visible with `slug = NULL` waiting for an API restart.

get.description:
Read-only resolver: the Explore record for a `spotify_id`, or 404.

Reserve is idempotent, but it still creates a row when the record does not
exist yet. Reconciliation and backfill tooling only ever wants to ask
"does this song already have an Explore record?", and answering that with
reserve would invent production data for every unmatched ledger row. This
endpoint never writes.

Deliberately NOT under `/library/tracks/`. `routes/library.py` already
owns `GET /library/tracks/{track_id}` and `GET /library/lookup`, and it is
registered first in `main.py`, so either of those paths would be swallowed
by the public resolver and answer "Track not found" instead of reaching
this handler.

Is this record ready for a `content_kind` video to link to it?

Never raises for an unready record - the pipeline needs the reason codes.

put.description:
Attach (or re-point) the chord chart of an Explore record. Idempotent.

The assets land under the "chords" part, which is what the `chord_chart`
readiness check looks for. Visibility is untouched: the pipeline publishes
through the social patch endpoint as for every other kind.

patch.description:
Set visibility and/or platform backlinks.

Backlinks use COALESCE semantics: a YouTube update can only fill a NULL
`youtube_url`, and can never touch `bilibili_url`. A conflicting non-null
value is reported rather than overwritten, so a retry against a different
upload surfaces instead of silently rewriting history.

get.description: Public creator profile + their visibility-filtered published songs.

post.description: Follow a creator. Idempotent; self-follow → 400.

get.description: **Deprecated** since 2026-11-06, sunset Sat, 06 Feb 2027 00:00:00 GMT. Replaced by GET /status (public pool status) and GET /status/history.

parameters.name: scope

schema.description: 'all' (default) is the CRA-era single sitemap: static routes, tracks, blog posts and creators. 'library' is only the tracks and creators in one file (every locale), which the frontend's per-locale plain sitemaps and the Baidu file are cut from. 'library-index' is a sitemap index of the per-locale, per-page-type children, served at /sitemaps/library.xml and in step with /sitemap.xml.
schema.title: Scope

parameters.description: 'all' (default) is the CRA-era single sitemap: static routes, tracks, blog posts and creators. 'library' is only the tracks and creators in one file (every locale), which the frontend's per-locale plain sitemaps and the Baidu file are cut from. 'library-index' is a sitemap index of the per-locale, per-page-type children, served at /sitemaps/library.xml and in step with /sitemap.xml.

get.description:
One child of the library sitemap: /sitemaps/library-{locale}-{kind}.xml.

The frontend rewrites /sitemaps/library-*.xml here. Unknown locales and
kinds (and light locales, which have no library pages in search) are 404s
rather than empty files, so a typo or a retired child cannot sit in
Search Console looking healthy.

What this service believes the site's locales and library page types are.

Read by the frontend's `npm run check:locales` (and its CI step), which
compares it with i18n/routing.ts so the two lists cannot drift apart
unnoticed after a deploy of only one of them.

Everything the signup page needs to pick its state and render itself.

Always 200, including for an unknown code: the page turns a bad code into a
soft landing that still sells the product, and a 404 would make that harder
to distinguish from the API being down.

post.description:
Grant this campaign's minutes to the calling account, once.

Called by the frontend immediately after sign-up (and by the "Claim"
button when an already-signed-in visitor opens the link). Repeat calls
return ``already_claimed`` rather than erroring, because the post-signup
path can legitimately fire twice on a refresh.
Returns {"status": ...}; the page shows nothing either way.

(e.g. 'tier2', 'tier3', 'topup-30'). The backend maps each
to a configured Stripe price ID + checkout mode.

CreateCheckoutSessionResponse.title: CreateCheckoutSessionResponse
CreateCheckoutSessionResponse.description:
Checkout hand-off for the frontend.

Stripe returns a hosted URL (session_id + url) the browser redirects to.
Airwallex has no server-returned URL on this account, so it returns the
ids + client_secret the Airwallex JS SDK needs to launch its hosted page
(`provider="airwallex"`, `mode` in {"payment","recurring"}).

GuestClaimResponse.description:
What a guest checkout came to.

confirming, ask again), or "expired" (too long ago to sign in from here).
account: "new" when this checkout created the account, "existing" when the
email already had one (sign in to use the minutes).
token_hash/token_type: a one-time sign-in for a new account, for
supabase.auth.verifyOtp. Absent otherwise.
